source.title: Behavioral variability through stochastic choice and its gating by anterior cingulate cortex

confidence_rationale: The closest mapping in this directory to what ARC-055 actually means by V(t): not confidence in a choice, but an estimate of whether the internal model is tracking the environment at all, causally controlling whether that model is permitted to drive selection. Circuit-specific perturbation in transgenic rats showed that switching between a strategic, history- and model-based mode and a stochastic mode in which action-outcome history is ignored is controlled by locus coeruleus input to anterior cingulate cortex. Confidence 0.71 rather than higher because the output is a binary-ish MODE switch rather than the graded influence on trajectory ranking ARC-055 describes, because the gating quantity is inferred from the behavioural regime rather than measured as an explicit signal, and because I worked from the abstract and secondary sources rather than the full text -- the specific perturbation directions are stated here only at the level the abstract supports.
failure_signatures: The demonstrated output is a switch between two behavioural REGIMES -- model-guided versus history-ignoring -- not a graded modulation of which trajectory is selected. ARC-055 asserts V(t) influences E3 trajectory selection, which most naturally reads as continuous re-ranking. A binary gate that disconnects the model wholesale is a weaker and architecturally different mechanism, and if that is all the biology implements then ARC-055's graded formulation is over-specified.

The quantity doing the gating is not measured as an explicit signal in this study; it is inferred from the fact that animals enter the stochastic mode when the environment defeats counter-prediction. ARC-055 turns on the distinction between an explicit signal and an emergent epiphenomenon, and a regime change identified behaviourally does not by itself adjudicate that distinction -- the same data are compatible with noradrenergic drive raising processing noise until the model's influence is swamped, with no explicit validity signal represented anywhere.

Converging evidence from Kane et al. 2017 (Cogn Affect Behav Neurosci, DREADD stimulation of locus coeruleus in a patch-foraging task) found that earlier patch-leaving under increased LC tonic activity was best explained by an increase in decision noise rather than a systematic shift in the leaving threshold. If disengagement is implemented by noise injection rather than by a represented signal entering the selection computation, that is a live alternative architecture in which ARC-055's availability requirement is unnecessary.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Rats facing a virtual competitor use history- and model-based strategies, but switch to a stochastic mode -- in which outcomes associated with their own actions are ignored and normal engagement of anterior cingulate cortex is suppressed -- when the competitor cannot be defeated by counter-prediction. Circuit perturbations in transgenic rats demonstrated that switching between strategic and stochastic modes is controlled by locus coeruleus input into anterior cingulate cortex. The authors conclude that under uncertainty about environmental rules, changes in noradrenergic input alter ACC output and prevent erroneous beliefs from guiding decisions, enabling behavioural variation.
mapping.ree_translation: Of the five entries now in this directory, this one maps most directly onto what ARC-055 means by verisimilitude. The other four concern confidence in a decision -- how likely this particular choice is to be correct. Verisimilitude, as ARC-055 uses it, is a different quantity: how well the internal model corresponds to the world. That is exactly the quantity at issue here. The animal's model of the competitor is either tracking or it is not, and the authors' own formulation -- preventing erroneous beliefs from guiding decisions -- is a statement that an estimate of model validity determines whether the model is allowed to drive action selection. Mapped onto ARC-055: when V(t) is low, the E3 selector stops taking the generative model's trajectory rankings at face value. The evidence is causal and circuit-specific rather than correlational, which is what the selection leg most needed, and it lands on selection rather than on report or on learning rate. It also supplies something the other entries do not, which is a functional rationale for why an architecture would want V(t) on the selection path at all: not to sharpen a good model's choices, but to disengage a bad model before it commits the agent to trajectories it has no business trusting. That is closer to ARC-055's kappa_commit -- a threshold below which commitment should not occur -- than anything else in the directory.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This entry bears on the SELECTION leg; it does not re-evidence the learning leg. The central caveat is granularity. ARC-055 describes V(t) as influencing E3 trajectory selection, which reads as graded re-ranking of candidate trajectories; what is demonstrated here is a switch between two regimes, one model-guided and one in which action-outcome history is ignored altogether. A wholesale gate and a graded weight are different architectures, and this study evidences the former. Second, the gating quantity is not observed as an explicit signal -- it is inferred from the behavioural regime the animal occupies -- so the study does not adjudicate ARC-055's explicit-signal-versus-epiphenomenon commitment, which is the claim's load-bearing distinction. A reading in which noradrenergic drive simply raises processing noise until the model's influence is swamped is compatible with these data and requires no represented validity signal; Kane et al. 2017, using DREADD stimulation of locus coeruleus in a patch-foraging task, found exactly that noise-based signature for a related disengagement effect. Third, this assessment rests on the published abstract and secondary sources, not the full text; the perturbation directions are characterised here only as far as the abstract licenses. Rat, adversarial competitive task, single laboratory.
mapping.source_context: Transgenic rats in a competitive game against virtual opponents of varying defeatability, with behavioural strategy modelling; circuit-specific perturbation of the locus coeruleus projection to anterior cingulate cortex, with ACC engagement assessed across strategic and stochastic behavioural modes.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.85: Cell, circuit-specific perturbation in transgenic animals rather than pharmacological or regional inactivation, with a behavioural-modelling account of the two modes and a task designed so that the switch is adaptive rather than a deficit. Mapping fidelity 0.72, weighted heavily per the arch_commitment convention: this is the best verisimilitude-as-model-validity mapping in the directory and the quantity is right, but the mechanism demonstrated is a mode gate rather than the graded influence ARC-055 specifies, and the gating quantity is inferred behaviourally rather than measured. Transfer risk 0.35: rat, adversarial competitive task; the trajectory space is richer than a 2AFC but the mode-switch framing may not survive transfer to graded trajectory selection. Aggregate 0.71, held marginally below Zajkowski despite higher source quality because the mode-versus-graded mismatch bites directly on how ARC-055 is worded.
